item.title:
Last night in Brooklyn, masked demonstrators marched through a heavily Jewish neighborhood, past Jewish homes and families, toward a Jewish house of worship, chanting for intifada, waving a Hezbollah flag, and screaming abuse at Jews in the street.
This was not a protest. It was targeted harassment of a minority community.
And it was not spontaneous. The organizations behind the march - PAL-Awda, the Palestinian Youth Movement, and Within Our Lifetime - have stated explicitly that they will "show up whenever and wherever" Jewish events occur.
Their goal is clear: to suppress Jewish life and Jewish civil rights.
New York's leaders - Zohran Mamdani, take note - need to stop pretending this is normal protest activity. It is not about Israel. It is a pretext to target Jews where they live.
Jewish New Yorkers are entitled to live openly, safely, and proudly in their own communities. They should not have to rely on heavy police deployments just to preserve the basic dignity of Jewish communal life.
We have a moral responsibility to say: no more.

item.title:
🇦🇹 Almost half of muslim immigrant youth in Austria believe that their religious rules are above the law
A new Vienna-commissioned study reveals that 41% of Muslim immigrant youth (aged 14–24) believe Islamic religious rules take precedence over Austrian national law.
- 64% of respondents agreed that Islamic rules govern all aspects of daily life and must be strictly observed.
- 53% of participants believe that every Muslim woman should wear a headscarf in public spaces.
- 39% of those surveyed expressed that all people should follow the rules of Islam.
- 43% of the young respondents hold Western nations responsible for the current crises facing the Islamic world.
According to data published by Die Presse, Muslims now constitute up to 49% of all public school students in Vienna, outnumbering Catholics (17%), Orthodox Christians (14%), and non-affiliated students (23%).
